first.rationale: The two live symptoms — onboarding completion -4% QoQ and activation -6% QoQ — are plausibly linked, with onboarding completion upstream of activation. memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) and memory_91 (in-product activation messaging lifted week-one engagement) are the two directly on-point priors, so those are the two worth spending archive pulls on: I want the original effect sizes, the population they were run on, and whether the onboarding result was measured through to activation or only to completion. If memory_86's record shows the lift propagated to activation, simplify_onboarding dominates because it treats both declines with one slot; if it stopped at completion, I would switch the slot to activation_messaging per memory_91. I am deliberately NOT choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing being the loudest signal: memory_73 records that it acquired revenue but materially cut 30-day retention and explicitly warns against generalizing it, which is disqualifying against a sustainable long-term qualified-revenue objective — reacting to a competitor is exactly the generalization that memory warns about. referral_incentive (memory_57) targets established customers and does not address the activation/onboarding funnel decline; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a different segment from the SMB accounts under pressure. Downstream value risk is real and flagged: memory_31 achieved its lift by cutting required signup fields, and stripping qualification fields can degrade lead scoring, segmentation, and routing — i.e. it can raise raw activation while lowering *qualified* revenue, the actual objective. So the experiment must be instrumented on downstream qualified-pipeline and 30/60-day retention, not just completion rate, and I would prefer trimming or deferring fields over deleting the qualification signal. Uncertainty preserved: all six memories are consolidated summaries whose confidence intervals and baseline conditions I cannot see, and they were formed on days 12-61 under a pre-competitor market; the current environment is materially different, so these priors are directional inputs rather than settled facts. Standard experiment scale with a holdout and explicit retention/qualified-revenue guardrails, escalating only if the guardrails hold.

final.rationale: I precommitted to a switch condition and the archive triggered it. exp_86 is confirmed and genuinely strong (completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, 30-day retention +3%) but it does NOT report activation — the chain stops at completion and time-to-value. The inference that onboarding completion propagates to activation was my assumption, not a measured result, and the source record declines to support it. exp_91, by contrast, measures activation directly: activation +6%, week-one engagement +11%, retention +1%, confirmed. The activation decline (-6% QoQ) is both the larger of the two symptoms and the one with a directly measured remedy of matching magnitude, so activation_messaging is the choice with the shortest inferential distance to the actual gap. Secondary reason to prefer it: it is an in-product intervention that touches no signup or qualification fields, so it avoids the downstream value risk I flagged earlier — memory_31's mechanism was cutting required fields, which trades lead-qualification signal for raw activation and can raise activation while lowering *qualified* revenue. activation_messaging carries no such trade. Promotional_pricing remains excluded despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records a material 30-day retention loss and an explicit instruction not to generalize it, which is disqualifying against a sustainable long-term qualified-revenue objective. referral_incentive and enterprise_sales_assist address neither declining metric in the affected segment. Downstream value risk flagged and instrumented: 'week-one engagement' and 'first meaningful action' are proxy metrics that in-product nudges are unusually good at inflating without creating real value, so success criteria must be 30/60-day retention and qualified pipeline, not the nudge-adjacent metrics themselves; I want a holdout and a check that lifted accounts are not simply clicking through prompts. Uncertainty preserved: exp_91's +6% was measured on a pre-competitor population around day 61, and the current environment includes active price-driven churn pressure that messaging cannot address — a full +6% recovery should not be assumed, and if activation is being driven by accounts leaving for the competitor rather than by weak onboarding, this experiment will correctly show a null and that is informative. simplify_onboarding is not discarded; it is the strongest candidate for next week's slot, and it is worth measuring activation end-to-end there since exp_86 never did.
